title: ToolApiV1dot10
description: K-09 Tool API v1.10, a minor version that only adds (T-1373; T-1358's NEED, DL-743; CQ-313; README 'v1.10'): recordSafetyOutcome's answer names every outbox row the record's commit writes, each with its recipient handle, so the handle actor can wake each recipient's run at once (RULES 4.12: 'Danger now: the safety message first ..., then a person is told at once'; arch 06 line 329: crisis words, Rosie's team and the owner at once; an emergency or a threat, the owner). It adds safetyLine.recipientHandleId, the handle the line's row goes to, and safetyRows, each row the commit writes with its recipient handle, its send class and what it carries (the line's text row, its email copy or its one row by email; the hand-off's alert; a team page's rows), on first and repeated answers alike. A safety run names its recipient (K-05 v1.14 default 134) and the actor knows only its own handle, so without them a row to anyone else waits for that person's next run (T-1358's finding). It only adds to v1.9 (tool-api.v1.9.schema.json, frozen by T-054 and unchanged, referred to here, which refers to v1.8 and down to v1): every v1.9 definition is here under its own name, 423 of them by reference; the two changed ones, recordSafetyOutcome.response (v1.1's fields restated with the same keywords, with the two new optional fields a v1.10 call always returns) and recordSafetyOutcome.exchange (which takes it, and holds a call with no turn to no row: K-04 outbox_rows.turn_id is not null), take every earlier value, so every v1 to v1.9 exchange is a v1.10 exchange. Added: safetyRowWritten. No call, key or error is added, so callName is v1.9's. A record's hand-off alert and team page rows are send class safety (CQ-313 question 1; README default 176). Not model-facing, so number and length limits are schema rules here. Owner: the architect.

recordSafetyOutcome.response.title: RecordSafetyOutcomeResponse
recordSafetyOutcome.response.description: The outcome, its hold, its line and who is told, as v1.1 has them (gives and hold.version included), with two optional fields a v1.10 call always returns, together (T-1373; README 'v1.10', defaults 174 to 178): safetyLine.recipientHandleId, the handle the line's row goes to, and safetyRows, every outbox row the record's commit writes, each with its recipient handle, its send class and what it carries; a repeat names the first record's rows (default 175). A v1 to v1.9 call leaves both out.

outcomes.description: What holds after code's rules (K-02 v1 safetyResult.outcomes).

hold.description: The hold on routine actions, or null when the outcome holds nothing (No, with no stop words).

releaseRule.description: K-34 v1 safety_holds.release_rule: the strictest of its outcomes (arch 06 line 327).

blocksBooking.description: Plug-in stop words matched: they still block booking after an at-once release (A3-26).

version.description: v1.1: the hold row's version (K-34 v1 safety_holds.version): 1 for the hold this call wrote (K-34 v1 rule 2: version integer not null default 1), its stored version on a repeat. releaseSafetyHold's expectVersion names it. Left out only by a v1 call.

safetyLine.description: The outcome step's checked line, or null for No (v1); from v1.10 with the handle its row goes to.

outboxRowId.description: The outbox row of send class safety, or null when the actor already sent it (sentByActor) or the caller is a page or an agent, which shows it (v1); a read that timed out with no danger word gets the outage line, whose row is send class quick_reply (v1.1). With an email copy beside it, the text row; for the email way, the one row by email (README default 174).

recipientHandleId.description: v1.10: the handle outboxRowId goes to (K-04 outbox_rows.recipient_handle_id), a handle's id and never a number or an address (K-08 v1 handleRef; README default 177): the writer's handle the reach card picks, or the handle the text came from when there is no card (README default 174, open gap 144), or for a threat the owner's (A3-48; S13-10: no safety message to the one who threatens). Null exactly when outboxRowId is null. Left out only by a v1 to v1.9 call.

told.description: Who is told and through which row (arch 06 line 329).

who.description: The owner, whoever the owner named, or Rosie's team (arch 06 line 329; Q-18: Jay and the CTO until launch).

via.description: The row that tells them: a hand-off (K-36 v1 hand_offs), a page (team_pages) or a harm report (K-34 v1 harm_reports).

nothingBooks.description: true when danger holds: for a page or an AI, the safety message is returned and nothing books (arch 02 line 129).

repeated.description: true when this event id was recorded before.

gives.description: v1.1: the key the call wrote, safe (A3-22, B3-17: K-34 the turn's safety outcome; 02-contracts section 8), for every outcome row, No included. Left out only by a v1 call.

safetyRows.description: v1.10: every outbox row the record's commit writes, in commit order (its line's rows, then the rows of who is told), each with the handle it goes to, its send class and what it carries (safetyRowWritten; README default 174). A repeat writes nothing and names the rows the first record wrote, the same list in the same order (README default 175), so a repeated answer wakes them again and nothing goes twice (K-07 v1's keys). Empty when the commit writes no outbox row: No, the actor's own send, a call with no turn (README default 178), a line nothing can carry. The handle actor wakes each distinct recipient of its safety rows at once, never gated (T-1375; K-05 v1.14 item 67). Left out only by a v1 to v1.9 call.
A v1.10 answer names the line's recipient beside its rows.

allOf.description: A line with its recipient comes with the rows: v1.10 returns both or neither.

The line's own rows are named exactly when it has a row: a line with an outbox row is among the rows, as writtenFor line (README default 174); a line with none (No, the actor's own send, a page's or an agent's call) names no line row.

safetyRowWritten.title: SafetyRowWritten
safetyRowWritten.description: v1.10 (T-1373; README defaults 174 to 177): one outbox row a recordSafetyOutcome commit writes, named with the handle it goes to, so the handle actor can wake that recipient's run at once (T-1358's finding; RULES 4.12; arch 06 line 329). Its id (K-04 outbox_rows.id), its recipient (outbox_rows.recipient_handle_id: a handle's id, never a number or an address, K-08 v1 handleRef), its send class (K-07 v1 sendClass) and what it carries: line (the outcome step's checked line, or a timed-out read's outage line: its text row, its email copy, or its one row by email for the email way, as the reach card has it; a threat's line goes to the owner), handOff (the hand-off's alert to the person told: v1 handOff.response.alertOutboxRowId) or teamPage (one row of a team page opened at once, to one member of Rosie's team: v1 pageTeam.response.outboxRowIds). A record tells only for crisis words, an emergency or a threat, so its alert and page rows are send class safety (README default 176, CQ-313 question 1): the person told is told at once, at any hour (RULES 4.12; RULES 4.3). The line's rows are safety, or quick_reply for the outage line (v1.1).

recipientHandleId.description: The handle it goes to (K-04 outbox_rows.recipient_handle_id): a handle's id, never the raw number or address (K-08 v1 handleRef; README default 177). An email row's recipient is the email handle's id.

sendClass.description: The row's send class (K-07 v1 sendClass; K-04 outbox_rows.send_class).

writtenFor.description: What the row carries: line (the record's checked line or outage line, each row of it), handOff (the hand-off's alert) or teamPage (a team page's row to one member).

recordSafetyOutcome.exchange.title: RecordSafetyOutcomeExchange
recordSafetyOutcome.exchange.description: One recordSafetyOutcome request with its outcome: v1's, or the handle actor's record on arrival (v1.1), its answer from v1.10 able to name each row the commit writes with its recipient (safetyRows). A call with no turn (caller.turnId null: a page's or an agent's free text, a job) writes no outbox row (K-04 outbox_rows.turn_id is not null), so its answer names none (README default 178).

allOf.description: A call with no turn names no row (README default 178).
